title: Handle every union member
summary: Use a discriminated union and an exhaustive switch so a missing event cannot ship.

scenario.briefing: The activity feed receives order, refund, and visit events. A formatter handles two kinds and labels every visit as unknown. Add the missing branch and make future omissions fail at compile time.

objectives.description: Handle every member of the event union.
Explain discriminated unions and exhaustive checks.

hints: The union already declares a visit member with a count field.
Add a case for event.kind equal to visit.
Return a string that includes event.count.
Use a never assignment in the default branch to catch future members.

misconceptions.description: Falling through to a default for an unhandled member.
misconceptions.feedback: A default that returns a generic label hides missing behavior. Handle visit explicitly and use never in the default.

misconceptions.description: Believing a type assertion validates the runtime shape.
misconceptions.feedback: An assertion is erased and does not check the value. Narrow with kind checks or a runtime guard.

sections.title: A literal property discriminates a union
sections.body: A union whose members share a literal property such as kind is a discriminated union. Checking event.kind narrows the value to the member with that literal, so each branch sees only the fields that member declares.

sections.title: Exhaustiveness is a compile-time check
sections.body: A switch over every kind can end with a default that assigns the remaining value to never. If a new member is added and a branch is missing, the assignment stops compiling. This turns an easy-to-miss runtime gap into a build error.

sections.title: Assertions do not close a union
sections.body: A type assertion tells the compiler to trust the author. It does not add a missing branch or validate an external value. Runtime boundaries still need guards, and local unions should be handled with checks and exhaustive switches.

steps.title: Narrowing and exhaustiveness

statements.label: A literal kind property lets TypeScript narrow a discriminated union.
An exhaustive switch can use never to catch a missing case.
A type assertion proves the runtime shape of a value.
Adding a union member may require updating every exhaustive switch.

steps.explanation: A discriminator narrows the union, and a never assignment makes omissions compile errors. Assertions do not validate runtime data.
hints: An assertion is a compile-time claim, not a runtime check.
Exhaustiveness is what makes new members visible.
